lead: >-
  The Bolivia–Peru combination in Ada Tours' festive journeys usually means continuing a much longer itinerary after an event in Brazil. Carnival and the Champions' Parade take place in Rio de Janeiro, while New Year's Eve is celebrated on Copacabana. Travelers then cross Bolivia's Altiplano and visit Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu. Choose according to the main event's date and the sequence of high-altitude days.

## Bolivia and Peru on a festive journey: where does the event take place?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which **Bolivia and Peru are part of the main itinerary**, while an event determines the entire trip's calendar. An important detail: on the current programs in this combination, **the festive centerpiece is in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil**. The Bolivian and Peruvian days are devoted to the salt flat, archaeological monuments, cities and natural regions of the Andes.

This page is therefore most useful for a specific question: **how can you see Bolivia and Peru after Carnival or New Year without missing key stops or ascending too abruptly?** For routes without a festival focus, see [the general Bolivia and Peru catalog](/multi-country/bolivia_peru/); to compare events across country combinations, visit [multi-country festive tours](/multi-country/interests/events-and-festivals/).

## Choosing the event: Carnival or New Year

**["Five Latin American Countries with Rio Carnival: 18 Days"](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/)** begins in Rio with the Champions' Parade. The program states travel dates of **February 12 to March 1, 2027**. The itinerary then visits both sides of Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago, Atacama, Bolivia and Peru. In Bolivia, travelers cross the high-altitude regions by four-wheel drive, pass Uyuni and La Paz, then continue via Tiwanaku and Titicaca toward Cusco and Machu Picchu.

**["Best Sights of Five Countries in 19 Days"](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/)** is a private Carnival itinerary. The event takes place in the Rio de Janeiro section, after which the route continues through Iguazu and Argentina to Chile, Bolivia and Peru. The Bolivian leg includes lagoons and the salt flat, then La Paz and Tiwanaku. The Peruvian leg covers Puno, the Uros islands, Cusco and Machu Picchu.

**["New Year Tour of Five Latin American Countries for 19 Days"](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/)** is built around celebrating New Year on Copacabana. December 31 is devoted to Rio and the festive night; January 10–13 includes the crossing from Chile into Bolivia, Uyuni, La Paz and the journey to Titicaca, followed by Peru's cities and Machu Picchu.

| Festival | Format |
|---|---|
| [Champions' Parade in Rio](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) | Group, 18 days |
| [Rio Carnival](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) | Private, 19 days |
| [New Year on Copacabana](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) | Group, 19 days |

The description "festive tour through Bolivia and Peru" does not itself mean attending local festivals in La Paz, Puno or Cusco. For a specific Bolivian or Peruvian celebration, a separate itinerary must first confirm its name, location and date.

## Bolivia after the celebration: Atacama, lagoons and Uyuni

On all three programs, the Bolivian leg comes **after Chile's Atacama**. A central section is the crossing toward the high-altitude lagoons and [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Traveling across the Altiplano requires time: a tourist bus on a paved highway and an off-road journey through lagoons serve different purposes.

Travel conditions change markedly during this section of a festive journey. Warm, humid Rio gives way to open high-altitude landscapes with cold mornings, dry air and long transfers. On the New Year itinerary, the journey takes place in January, when the condition of the salt flat and its roads may differ from the dry season. Whether visitors can drive on a particular area, visit Incahuasi Island or see a mirror-like surface depends on conditions on the actual day.

The route then reaches [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and continues to [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) and the Peruvian shore of Lake Titicaca. Instead of counting towns on a map, consider **how much time remains for Uyuni itself and how many hours the cross-border journey takes**. Moving a flight may affect several subsequent itinerary days.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu as part of the longer itinerary

In Peru, the festive tours reach Puno and the Uros islands, then cross the Andean plateau to Cusco. The next major destination is [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). This is not an optional "day after the concert," but a substantial cultural and historical part of the journey.

Three transitions matter in practice. The first is entering Peru overland from Bolivia and taking the Titicaca excursion. The second is the road journey from Puno to Cusco with stops en route. The third is visiting Machu Picchu and returning in time for the onward flight to Lima. If you mainly want more time at archaeological sites, compare these days with [cultural and historical tours in Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/). The event-themed catalog serves a different purpose: linking a fixed festive date to an extensive journey across the continent.

On all three programs, Peru comes toward the end of a busy itinerary. The actual density of the preceding Bolivian days is therefore as important to rest and well-being as the trip's total duration.

## What to confirm before choosing a festive departure

A festive journey has **one fixed point in the calendar**. Carnival nights and New Year's Eve determine flight sequences; visits to Uyuni, Titicaca and Machu Picchu must fit the remaining time. When comparing tours, ask exactly which parade is included, what ticket category applies, when the high-altitude section begins and how much time is free after the major overnight event.

We help coordinate flights and international transfers, guided excursion formats and the sequence of natural and cultural activities. Entry rules must be checked against passengers' nationality and actual travel dates, while access conditions and ticket availability for individual attractions are confirmed when arranging the journey. **A Carnival ticket or a festive tour title does not automatically confirm every service across all five countries.**

For a separate comparison of tours where the celebration and city program are concentrated in one country, explore [event tours in Brazil](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/brazil/). [Theme-based tours through Bolivia](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/bolivia/) and [Peru](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/peru/) show which multi-country trips genuinely include them.

## Frequently asked questions about festive itineraries through Bolivia and Peru

### Do these tours include a festival in Bolivia or Peru itself?

On the featured programs, the main event takes place in **Rio de Janeiro**. Bolivia and Peru form part of the later itinerary, but the descriptions do not confirm attendance at local festivals in their cities.

### Which trip is suitable for the Champions' Parade?

[The 18-day Champions' Parade program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) explicitly names and includes the parade. Compare tickets and visit conditions with the particular offer, since different festive evenings at the Sambadrome are separate events.

### Can the trip be limited to Bolivia and Peru while keeping Carnival?

Carnival on these tours takes place in Brazil, with other principal countries between the celebration and Bolivia and Peru. Reducing the journey to two countries would require a different itinerary, not merely removing a few days.

### What makes the New Year version different?

On [the New Year tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/), the main celebration takes place on Copacabana, while Bolivia and Peru are visited in January. Carnival travel is tied to a February event; the remaining regions are largely similar, but dates and group format differ.

### What if Machu Picchu, rather than a festival, is my main goal?

Compare programs in [the Peru tour catalog](/peru/tour/). For this objective, the time spent in Peru, the itinerary through Cusco and tickets to the archaeological site matter more than attendance at a particular event in Brazil.

lead: >-
  On our itineraries through Bolivia and Peru, the culinary focus lies primarily in Peru: there is an opportunity for dinner at Central in Lima, and a longer private program includes lunches at MIL Centro near Moray and Wayra in the Sacred Valley. Bolivia adds a high-altitude journey through La Paz and Uyuni, but no dedicated Bolivian tastings are listed on these programs. ## What genuinely relates to gastronomy on journeys through Bolivia and Peru?

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring Bolivia and Peru on the main itinerary, with gastronomy listed among the travel interests. **This does not mean that wineries, cooking classes or separate culinary tours are scheduled in both countries.** The theme comes to life through the particular excursions, restaurants and optional services included in the programs.

The most substantial culinary experiences are in [Peru](/peru/): [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) and its contemporary restaurants, the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) with meals at specialist venues, and Andean cuisine alongside high-altitude historical landscapes. [Bolivia](/bolivia/) is represented by La Paz, Altiplano lakes and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). This is a compelling geographic extension, but on the tours listed, ordinary meals in Bolivia should be distinguished from dedicated culinary services.

## Where the actual culinary stops take place

On [the 18-day VIP Peru and Bolivia journey](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/), an evening transfer to Central restaurant in Lima is listed for a tasting dinner. **The dinner itself is not included** in the program price; the restaurant visit must be agreed when booking. This journey also features the Peruvian Amazon, Cusco, Titicaca and Bolivia's high-altitude lakes, so the restaurant evening forms only one part of a much wider itinerary.

[The extensive 33-day South America itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) includes meaningful lunch stops in Peru. Near [Moray](/peru/place/moray/) and [Maras](/peru/place/maras/), MIL Centro is listed, where the cuisine draws on Andean ingredients and ecosystems. The area around Pisac and Ollantaytambo features lunch at Wayra. This is a more appropriate option if gastronomy is meant to be a distinct travel experience. However, the route extends well beyond two countries: after Peru and Bolivia, it continues through Chile, including a visit to VIK winery. **Chilean wine should not be presented as a winery experience in Bolivia or Peru.**

The [12-day Chile–Bolivia–Peru itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/) has a different emphasis: Atacama, colorful lagoons, Uyuni, Tiwanaku and Machu Picchu. Wineries in the Maipo Valley are offered **as an extra in Chile**, not as an included tasting in either of the two countries featured in this selection.

The same distinction matters on [the 20-day, six-country journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/): its culinary possibilities are not equivalent to the MIL Centro restaurant program. Its days focus on sightseeing through several capitals and the Andes, while the wine excursion from Santiago is optional and takes place in Chile. Compare the actual day descriptions if gastronomy is the main purpose of your trip.

## Why it makes sense to consider Peru and Bolivia together

In Peru, restaurant experiences in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) can be combined with Andean culture in [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and a visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Bolivia extends the journey to [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) and Uyuni Salt Flat. For a food-focused traveler, the main trade-off is time: extra travel days and altitude reduce the time available for restaurants, markets and encounters with local cuisine.

MIL Centro lies at approximately 3,568 m near Moray. Therefore, after a flight from sea level, avoid scheduling a dense sequence of high-altitude excursions and long meals without time to acclimatize. Restaurant reservations, the journey from Cusco and menus should be agreed for the actual dates. Dinner in Lima and lunch in the Sacred Valley differ not just in cuisine but also in the logistical demands they create.

[The complete Bolivia and Peru tour selection](/multi-country/bolivia_peru/) includes journeys with other primary interests. If food matters more than visiting every natural attraction, also explore [food and wine tours involving Peru](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/peru/) and the general [multi-country gastronomy section](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/).

## Coordinating a culinary focus with the itinerary

Before booking, decide what is essential: **a restaurant dinner in Lima**, **lunch at MIL Centro or Wayra**, market visits, or simply opportunities to sample local food. You can then identify which itinerary provides enough time and which is actually focused on nature and archaeology. For any specific restaurant, confirm table availability, menu, payment and transfers separately, as well as whether the service is included in the chosen tour price.

We help combine restaurant reservations with excursions, flights and road transfers, distribute high-altitude days and arrange a sensible Peru–Bolivia sequence. But **included meals** and **optional culinary services** are different items: the final inclusions are defined by the conditions of the particular program, not the thematic catalog title.

## Frequently asked questions about gastronomy in Bolivia and Peru

### Do these tours feature wine tastings in Bolivia?

No separate Bolivian wine tasting is listed on the reviewed programs. Some longer itineraries offer wineries in **Chile** as an optional excursion; that country must be accounted for separately.

### Can I visit MIL Centro on an ordinary group tour?

MIL Centro is listed in the 33-day private itinerary. It cannot automatically be added to a short group program: separate logistics, reservations and free time must be confirmed.

### Is dinner at Central included in the VIP tour price?

No. [The 18-day Peru and Bolivia program](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/) includes a transfer to dinner, but the meal itself is identified as a separately paid service.

### Should I limit a culinary journey to Peru or add Bolivia?

If your main goal is particular restaurants in Lima and the Sacred Valley, a shorter Peru itinerary leaves more time for them. Bolivia is worth adding for Uyuni, the Altiplano and wider Andean geography, with extra transfers and altitude taken into account.

targetPath: /multi-country/bolivia_peru/interests/nature/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore the nature of Bolivia and Peru"
lead: >-
  Peru and Bolivia share the Andes, but the natural experiences offered by their itineraries differ: mountain valleys around Machu Picchu, high-altitude Lake Titicaca, the white Uyuni Salt Flat and the colorful lagoons of the Altiplano. We compare short journeys with itineraries covering southwestern Bolivia in full, explaining altitude demands and seasonal differences.
---

## Nature in Bolivia and Peru: Titicaca, Uyuni and the high Andes

Peru and Bolivia are linked by the Andes, Lake Titicaca and the history of ancient civilizations. For nature travel, however, it is especially important to distinguish three landscapes. In Peru, the route may wind through green mountain slopes and terraces around [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). High-altitude Titicaca lies along the border between the countries. Farther into Bolivia begin the immense salt expanses of [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and, on longer itineraries, colorful lagoons, geysers and desert plateaus.

It is rarely possible to explore these sites at a relaxed pace in just a few days. [The Peru and Bolivia tour catalog](/multi-country/bolivia_peru/) includes relatively short journeys featuring Titicaca as well as longer trips visiting Uyuni. Having two countries in the tour title does not in itself mean the salt flat is included.

## What to choose: three levels of exploring nature

### The Andes and Titicaca without Uyuni

["Enchanting Peru and Bolivia: 10 Days in the Andes"](/multi-country/tour/enchanted-peru-bolivia-10-days/) connects Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu, the journey to Puno, Copacabana, the Island of the Sun and La Paz. Its nature component centers on mountain valleys, passes along the Andean road and the large high-altitude lake.

One important distinction: **Uyuni Salt Flat is not part of this ten-day itinerary**. This tour is suitable for travelers who want to combine Peru's attractions with the Bolivian side of Titicaca without long additional journeys into southwestern Bolivia.

### Machu Picchu, Titicaca and the salt flat

["Peru and Bolivia with Uyuni Salt Flat: 12 Days in the Andes"](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) adds a separate Uyuni stage to Peru's sights and Lake Titicaca. Colchani and Incahuasi Island are included, with lunch and sunset viewing on the salt flat. This works for those eager to see the characteristic white salt surface but not planning an extended multi-day journey across every lagoon of the Altiplano.

In photographs, Uyuni sometimes looks like a mirrored plain and sometimes a dry surface of white salt polygons. Its appearance depends on season and weather. Including Uyuni on the itinerary does not guarantee a mirror effect on a particular date.

### Colorful lagoons and Altiplano geysers

[The 15-day "Uyuni and the Lakes of the Altiplano" itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) takes the nature section beyond the salt flat. Alongside Uyuni and Incahuasi, its route continues through the Siloli area to [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), Sol de Mañana geysers, Polques hot springs and [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/).

Here travelers see a whole chain of high-altitude ecosystems: salt flats, desert valleys, mineral lakes and geothermal areas. The trade-off is long road journeys and time at considerable elevation, often far from major settlements.

| Itinerary | Nature experiences |
|---|---|
| [10 days](/multi-country/tour/enchanted-peru-bolivia-10-days/) | Andes and Titicaca |
| [12 days](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) | Titicaca and Uyuni |
| [15 days](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) | Uyuni, lagoons and geysers |

## Altitude differences: the main planning factor

The mountain regions around Cusco, Titicaca and the Bolivian Altiplano lie far above sea level. On the journey, both temperatures and the elevation of overnight stays and walks change. Rapid ascent can cause altitude sickness even in physically fit travelers.

When choosing a tour, trace the arrival sequence, overnight stays and outings: how much time is allocated to adjusting to altitude, when the highest sites are visited and whether any days are relatively restful. If you have chronic medical conditions or previous altitude difficulties, seek medical advice before travel. Do not try to compensate for an overcrowded itinerary by speeding up transfers.

A visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) must also be distinguished from a multi-day trek along Inca trails. These have different fitness and booking requirements; admission to the archaeological complex does not confirm an included hike.

## Seasons: greenery in Peru and water on Uyuni

Around Cusco and Machu Picchu, the rainy season usually runs from November to March; the drier months are often better for mountain routes. Machu Picchu also lies among varied mountain and humid ecosystems, so its scenery differs from the exposed Altiplano.

During wetter months at Uyuni, a thin layer of water can appear, creating the famous reflection of the sky. In the dry season, geometric salt patterns are more visible, and certain vehicle routes are easier to plan. Too much water can alter some salt-flat routes; access to Incahuasi and other points depends on actual conditions.

No single month guarantees clear Andean weather, a mirrored Uyuni and unrestricted access to every mountain road. When choosing dates, decide what matters most: trekking, views of mountain valleys or reflections on the salt flat.

## The journey through Titicaca and itinerary logistics

[Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) introduce the Peruvian stage: some tours visit the Uros reed islands and Taquile. On the Bolivian side of [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), the route can lead via Copacabana to the Island of the Sun. Crossing between the countries requires time for border controls and the journey to La Paz.

The La Paz–Uyuni journey is another distinct transport stage, not a short excursion from the lake. On the extended lagoon itinerary, check the vehicle type, overnight arrangements and warm clothing requirements: temperatures can drop sharply at altitude after sunset.

Compare similar alternatives in [Peru nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/peru/) and [Bolivia nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/). If you wish to add another country and the Atacama Desert, check for it only in the actual [multi-country nature programs](/multi-country/interests/nature/), not as an automatic continuation of any Uyuni tour.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Peru and Bolivia

### Do all Peru–Bolivia tours include Uyuni?

No. For instance, [the ten-day program](/multi-country/tour/enchanted-peru-bolivia-10-days/) visits Cusco, Titicaca and La Paz without the salt flat. To see Uyuni, choose a tour with that stage.

### How does the 12-day tour differ from the 15-day tour?

[The 12-day option](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) includes the salt flat and Incahuasi; [the 15-day option](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) continues to the colorful lagoons, geysers and springs in southwestern Bolivia.

### Can I be certain of seeing Uyuni's mirror-like surface?

No. Reflections depend on water levels and weather. Choose the season with an understanding that the route may be adjusted to actual conditions.

### Is acclimatization needed for this trip?

Yes. Altitude planning is especially important around Titicaca and the Bolivian Altiplano. Review overnight stays and the ascent sequence on your chosen itinerary, taking personal medical limitations into account.

targetPath: /multi-country/bolivia_peru/interests/wildlife/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore wildlife watching in Bolivia and Peru"
lead: >-
  Nature journeys through Bolivia and Peru cover Lake Titicaca, Uyuni Salt Flat, Altiplano lagoons and, on some itineraries, the Peruvian Amazon. These ecosystems call for different amounts of time, preparation and travel pace. Compare which stops are included in current tours and where wildlife encounters are possible.
---

## Which nature regions do Bolivia and Peru connect?

Our themed selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with planned wildlife-watching activities. On [the 18-day itinerary featuring the Aria Amazon cruise](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/), those days take place in the Peruvian Amazon. Other nature programs in both countries are compared below. [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) introduce a high-altitude lake and its surroundings, [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) a vast salt flat, and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) the ecosystem of mountain lakes. Stops in the Peruvian Amazon appear only on certain longer itineraries.

Nature landscapes and wildlife watching should be distinguished. The "Nature" interest covers lakes, salt flats and mountain scenery; "Wildlife and Safaris" means planned observation of animals. A trip to a salt flat or waterfall does not itself establish such an activity or guarantee encounters with rare species.

## Titicaca: the lake environment of two countries

On the Peruvian side, some routes pass through [Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and the floating Uros islands; on the Bolivian side they visit [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/) and [the Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/). Local communities' culture is experienced alongside lake scenery. Birdwatching needs its own time and suitable excursion, not merely a drive along the shore.

On [the ten-day "Enchanting Peru and Bolivia" tour](/multi-country/tour/enchanted-peru-bolivia-10-days/), Titicaca is linked to Cusco, Machu Picchu and La Paz. This is a journey through diverse Andean scenery with a "Nature" theme; it does not form part of this wildlife-watching selection. A specialized birding itinerary would require checking the actual activities scheduled for each day.

## Uyuni: the salt flat and the lagoons offer different experiences

[Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) impresses with the geometry of its salt surface, reflections after rain and islands within the flat. To experience high-altitude fauna, however, continuing to the lagoons matters most.

For example, ["Peru and Bolivia with Uyuni: 12 Days"](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) includes Peru's cultural stops, Titicaca and the salt-flat area. ["Uyuni and the Lakes of the Altiplano"](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) continues farther through [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/) and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Flamingos may be seen around these lakes, but their presence and distance from visitors depend on natural conditions. Visitors must observe the rules of protected areas.

If the salt flat itself is your priority, a shorter option may be enough. If you are interested in lake ecosystems and birds, choose an itinerary that allocates separate days to the high-altitude lagoons.

## Peru's Amazon: a different climate and travel format

[The 18-day "Machu Picchu, Amazon and Uyuni" journey](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/) includes Iquitos and an Aria Amazon cruise along the Peruvian part of the Amazon River. The itinerary then connects Cusco, Titicaca and Bolivia's Uyuni.

The Amazon section is **in Peru**. It must not be assigned to Bolivia or promised on every two-country tour. Tropical river travel calls for preparation for humidity, boat journeys, lightweight protective clothing and respectful wildlife watching. High-altitude lagoons require the opposite: warm layers, sun protection and time for long drives across the plateau.

## Choosing a specific tour

| Main goal | Current itinerary |
|---|---|
| Titicaca and an introduction to the Andes | ["Enchanting Peru and Bolivia"](/multi-country/tour/enchanted-peru-bolivia-10-days/) |
| Uyuni and high-altitude lagoons | ["Uyuni and the Lakes of the Altiplano"](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) |
| Amazon, Andes and Uyuni | ["Machu Picchu, Amazon and Uyuni"](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/) |

These are different nature goals, not three interchangeable programs: the first two tours fall under the "Nature" interest, while the Amazon cruise on the third includes separate wildlife-watching days. High-altitude lagoons are optional on the 18-day tour and must not be treated as an included extension to the cruise. Compare the number of actual nature days, transfers and excursion inclusions. The [general Bolivia + Peru selection](/multi-country/bolivia_peru/) contains tours with any theme; you can also choose [nature tours in Bolivia](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/) and [Peru](/interests/nature/tours/peru/).

## Altitude, season and preparation

Cusco, Titicaca, La Paz and the Altiplano lagoons are all at considerable elevations, so the ascent pace and acclimatization matter in practice. The humid Amazon calls for entirely different clothing and protection for belongings. Weather and road access cannot be assessed from one "Bolivia and Peru" forecast: use the date and specific itinerary segment.

Ada Tours helps distribute days among nature stops, arrange flights and road transfers, and clarify current conditions for visiting reserves. If the aim is to see certain birds or other animals, this must be discussed separately, because a standard nature excursion cannot guarantee a particular species.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife in Bolivia and Peru

### Where should I look for flamingos on these routes?

At certain lagoons on Bolivia's Altiplano, including around [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Choose a tour that actually visits the lakes; sightings are not guaranteed.

### Does every tour include the Amazon?

No. It appears, for example, on [the 18-day itinerary through Iquitos](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/). Many programs remain in the Andes and highland plateau.

### What is the difference between a trip to Uyuni and a lagoon itinerary?

[Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is primarily a salt flat, while [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and neighboring lakes are different natural areas where birdwatching is possible. Check the days and travel distances between them in the itinerary.

### Do I need to adapt to altitude if I am not trekking?

Yes. Considerable altitude can affect well-being even on ordinary vehicle excursions. The ascent pace and overnight sequence matter regardless of a tour's sporting difficulty.

lead: >-
  On Ada Tours' longer journeys, Uruguay, Bolivia and Peru are connected not by a direct transfer but by a route through Argentina and Chile. A day in Montevideo gives way to the high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni Salt Flat, then the road through Tiwanaku, Titicaca and Cusco to Machu Picchu. ## What Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay bring to a single journey

On the map, these three countries seem like distant points. [Uruguay](/uruguay/) faces the Atlantic coast and Río de la Plata, [Bolivia](/bolivia/) introduces the high landscapes of the Andes, and [Peru](/peru/) adds Inca monuments and a route from Lake Titicaca to Cusco. Combining them requires coordinating flights alongside gradual changes in elevation, climate and excursion types.

The current catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with these countries **on the principal itinerary**: [a 20-day six-country journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [a 32-day eight-country tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Both also include Brazil, Argentina and Chile. The longer option continues from Peru to Ecuador and Colombia.

The "Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay" selection therefore identifies actual tours that **visit all three countries**, not a promise of a ready-made journey restricted to those three states.

## From Montevideo to the Andes: why Argentina is part of the route

On both current programs, travelers reach [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) **by ferry from Buenos Aires**. They depart Argentina's capital in the morning, spend the day sightseeing in Uruguay and return in the evening. This is a good way to add another capital to the journey, but it does not replace a detailed exploration of Uruguay's wineries, beach resorts or inland regions.

Montevideo comes long before Peru. Between that day and high-altitude Bolivia, the actual itinerary includes [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a flight to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and travel via [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This sequence gradually shifts from city walks to remote desert roads.

In practice, allow time for **re-entering Argentina from Uruguay** and check documents for that second entry. The ferry has its own departure schedule, check-in arrangements and luggage rules. Do not expect an immediate flight connection after the excursion without accounting separately for transfers between the port and airport, immigration formalities and possible delays.

## Bolivia's Altiplano: reaching Uyuni via lagoons and desert

From Chile's Atacama, travelers continue through Bolivia in 4×4 vehicles. The itinerary includes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), hot springs, geothermal areas and a route past a series of high-altitude lagoons to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

This segment differs sharply from the Uruguayan day. Instead of urban transport, there are long transfers through remote areas and an overnight stay at altitude. One of the current programs explicitly mentions stretches above 4,000 m. Even without a lengthy trek, the elevation can cause illness. Rest, hydration, moderate exertion and medical advice where indicated matter more than trying to cover as many stops as possible.

In dry conditions, Uyuni is a seemingly endless white expanse; after rain, parts of it may display the celebrated mirror reflection of the sky. These conditions affect driving differently. When choosing dates, balance the desired landscape against actual access, excursion conditions and the ability to reach the planned islands within the salt flat. A single beautiful promotional photograph cannot represent the entire season.

The itinerary then includes a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and sightseeing around the city. The Bolivian stage ends with a cultural stop at [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). This archaeological site gives substance to the transition into Peru: travelers encounter ancient Andean culture before the Inca monuments of Cusco.

## Bolivia–Peru: the border, Titicaca and the road to Cusco

The transfer from La Paz via Tiwanaku reaches the border near Desaguadero. After checks, travelers continue to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The program includes a visit to [the Uros islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/), known for their traditional reed constructions.

This is a significant difference from flying straight to Cusco: the lake and its culture form a separate stop, giving travelers more time in the central Andes. Yet border formalities may take longer than the geographical distance suggests. Border-post operating hours, documents and time allowances for road conditions matter.

From Puno, visitors take a tourist bus to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), with stops along the way. The journey includes mountain passes, historical sites and lunch. It is not a short transfer: part of the day is spent on the road and exploring sights. Travelers who find long drives tiring should discuss the pace and stops when selecting a program.

Next comes a day at [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), excursions in Cusco and a flight to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). The 20-day tour ends in Peru's capital. On the 32-day itinerary, Ecuador, the Galápagos Islands and Colombia follow Lima. The extended version adds new regions; it does not guarantee extra days at Machu Picchu itself.

## Machu Picchu: an entrance ticket matters more than an empty schedule slot

Visiting Machu Picchu depends on the particular date, entry time and route through the archaeological site. Peru's Ministry of Culture operates an official ticketing platform where buyers choose an available circuit and time. Reserving a hotel or train ticket does not by itself guarantee the desired entrance slot.

Confirm this visit before finalizing the other internal flights and hotels. On both tours, the day is embedded in a dense sequence: Puno, the drive to Cusco, Machu Picchu, excursions in Cusco and then Lima. Moving the visit by a day may require shifting several neighboring bookings.

If Inca history is your main reason for traveling, decide first which monuments and Machu Picchu circuit you wish to see, then select the trip length. [Peru tours](/peru/tour/) offer more focused programs without a lengthy multi-country beginning.

## Entry requirements and documents: three countries, but more borders

Uruguay, Bolivia and Peru have their own immigration rules. The actual journey also includes **Brazil, Argentina and Chile**, while the 32-day version adds **Ecuador and Colombia**. Checking documents only for the three countries in the catalog title is therefore insufficient.

First establish every traveler's nationality, passport validity, ability to re-enter Argentina after visiting Montevideo, visa or permit needs in transit countries and requirements for minors. The overland Chile → Bolivia crossing and entry from Bolivia into Peru also need specific checks. Even when a short tourist visit is visa-free, immigration documents and the border authority's decision remain separate requirements.

We help review the crossing sequence, prepare a document checklist and allow time in the transport schedule. Visa requirements are set by governments; no tour organizer can guarantee permission to cross a border.

| Uruguay | Uruguayan peso (UYU) |
| Bolivia | Boliviano (BOB) |
| Peru | Peruvian sol (PEN) |

The full itinerary adds other national currencies. Plan the budget **by journey segment**. In Montevideo, the main consideration is personal expenses during one sightseeing day. On Bolivia's Altiplano, the question is what is included in the road program and how much cash may be needed far from cities. In Peru, account separately for possible personal spending on souvenirs, food and additional visits.

Exchange rates and card usability change. Do not assume that one foreign bank card will work in every city, let alone along a high-altitude road. Confirm its use with the issuing bank, and plan a cash reserve according to real expenses and safe storage conditions. Even if part of the tour is priced in US dollars, local currencies may still be needed during free time.

Compare total tour prices only after checking the included services and pricing basis: a per-person amount for double occupancy is not the same as a price per room or private group. Both current offers list four-star hotels and domestic flights, but other exclusions and tariff details must be read in the individual program.

## Weather, altitude and physical demands

Montevideo has a temperate coastal climate, while the Peruvian and Bolivian highlands experience much more marked day-to-night temperature changes. Even in a season when light clothing is comfortable in Uruguay, the Altiplano requires warm layers, wind and sun protection, and closed-toe shoes.

Do not base your packing only on Lima's or Cusco's forecast: distances and elevations are large, and the weather in [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) differs from that at [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The rainy season in the Andes can affect road transfers and visits to the salt flat. On a route covering several climate zones, choose dates around the main natural or cultural attraction, then assess the other segments.

Discuss tolerance for altitude with a doctor before travel if you have chronic conditions. Check the insurance policy's restrictions for high-altitude excursions, remote roads and evacuation. Baggage allowances must be verified for each flight: domestic South American flights may involve different airlines and ticket conditions.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay

### Can I visit only these three countries without Chile and Argentina?

Existing Ada Tours programs also pass through other countries. A journey restricted to the selected three requires a new transport plan and an individual quote.

### Is Uruguay a multi-day stay or an excursion?

On both itineraries, it is a one-day excursion to Montevideo, taking the ferry from Buenos Aires and returning to Argentina. There are no overnight stays in Uruguay.

### Does the itinerary pass through Lake Titicaca?

Yes. After La Paz and Tiwanaku in Bolivia, travelers cross the border and visit the Puno area before heading to Cusco.

### Can I move the Machu Picchu visit to a more convenient day?

That depends on official ticket availability for the required entry category, transport and hotels. On a multi-country journey, coordinate any such change with subsequent flights.

### What is the most demanding part of the journey?

For many travelers, the main challenge is combining long transfers and high-altitude travel in Bolivia and Peru with a busy flight schedule. Preparation includes acclimatization, suitable insurance and adequate time at borders.
